newsitem.title: CANADA: Senior Canadian official resigns over swastika.
newsitem.headline: Senior Canadian official resigns over swastika.

text.p: A top Canadian official, Quebec Lieutenant-Governor Jean-Louis Roux, resigned on Tuesday after revealing that he wore a swastika, the Nazi symbol, as a student 54 years ago.

Roux, the official representative in Quebec of Britain's Queen Elizabeth, who is Canada's head of state, announced in a one-sentence statement that he had submitted his resignation to Prime Minister Jean Chretien.

"Jean-Louis Roux submitted this morning, to the prime minister of Canada, the Right Honourable Jean Chretien, his resignation as lieutenant-governor of Quebec," the statement said. His post is largely ceremonial.
Roux, 74, said earlier he had drawn a swastika on his laboratory coat as a medical student in Montreal in 1942.

He also marched in an anti-draft demonstration during the Second World War that ended with demonstrators breaking the windows of Montreal shops bearing Jewish-sounding names, but said he did not take part in the vandalism.

The revelations were published in a magazine article last weekend and prompted outrage on Monday in Parliament from the official opposition, the Bloc Quebecois. Chretien's government defended Roux's actions as youthful indiscretions committed half a century ago.
